title: Drinking Milk: Fresh, Flavored, and Chocolate Milk
description: The Signature drinking milk is a layered Signature design: a chilled milk base, a Signature cocoa-honey ribbon, and a whipped milk cap, served in a tall glass so the layers stay visible until stirred. The base is whole milk kept ice cold. The ribbon is cocoa powder whisked with a little warm milk and honey until glossy, poured slowly so it sinks in a dark band. The cap is milk whipped with a spoon of cream until soft and spoonable, floated on top. The drink is stirred at the table, which blends the ribbon through the cold milk and gives a chocolate milk that is richer at the first sip and mellower at the last. It is a Signature original: the layering, the ribbon ratio, and the whipped cap are the design, not a record of a traditional recipe.
ingredients: 1 liter whole milk, pasteurized, kept ice cold
20 g cocoa powder, 30 g honey, and 60 ml warm milk for the ribbon
150 ml cold cream for the whipped cap
A pinch of cinnamon for the cap, optional
method: Whisk the cocoa, honey, and warm milk together until glossy and smooth, then cool the ribbon to room temperature.
Pour the cold milk into four tall glasses, filling each about three quarters full.
Spoon the ribbon slowly down the inside of each glass so it settles as a visible dark band.
Whip the cold cream until soft peaks form, spoon a cap onto each glass, and dust with cinnamon if wanted.
Serve at once with a long spoon and stir at the table to blend the layers.
safety: Use pasteurized milk. Honey is not for infants under 12 months. Milk allergy and lactose notes apply exactly as for plain drinking milk: this design does not remove milk protein or lactose.
storage: Assemble just before serving. The ribbon keeps covered in the refrigerator for 3 days; the whipped cap is best within a few hours and must stay cold.
variations: Signature iced ribbon milk: pour the ribbon over ice first, then the cold milk, and skip the cap.
Signature warm ribbon milk: warm the milk to about 60 degrees Celsius and pour the ribbon through it for a marbled effect.
Signature berry ribbon: replace half the cocoa with crushed berries for a fruit band.

title: Milk in Baking: Breads and Cakes
description: The Signature milk bake is a two-milk loaf and cake pair built around one Signature method: milk is used twice, once warm in the dough and once brushed on as a milk wash, so the crust stays soft and glossy. The Signature loaf adds a spoon of honey to the warm milk, which feeds the yeast and gives a faint sweetness. The Signature cake uses the same milk twice too: milk in the batter and a warm milk drizzle over the hot cake, which soaks in and keeps the crumb moist for days. The loaf and the cake share one dough-handling rhythm, knead until smooth, rise until doubled, and bake until golden, so a baker learns both from one practice. This is a Signature original design, not a traditional recipe record.
ingredients: 500 g bread flour
300 ml warm milk (35 to 40 degrees Celsius)
15 g honey
7 g instant yeast
10 g salt
30 g butter, softened
60 ml extra milk for brushing and drizzling
method: Stir the honey and yeast into the warm milk and rest for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour and salt, add the milk mixture and butter, and knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth.
Cover and rise for 60 to 90 minutes until doubled, then shape into a loaf in a greased tin.
Rise again for 30 to 45 minutes, brush the top with milk, and bake at 190 degrees Celsius for 30 to 35 minutes.
For the Signature cake, bake the milk cake as usual, then drizzle 60 ml warm milk over the hot cake and cool in the tin.
Brush the loaf once more with milk while warm for a soft, glossy crust.
safety: Use pasteurized milk. Honey is not for infants under 12 months. Baked milk still contains milk protein, so this design is not safe for a person with milk allergy.
storage: The Signature loaf keeps sealed for 2 to 3 days at room temperature or frozen sliced for up to a month. The drizzled cake keeps covered for 3 days, refrigerated after the first day.
variations: Signature honey-milk rolls: shape the loaf dough into rolls, brush twice with milk, and bake 15 to 18 minutes.
Signature milk-wash buns: skip the honey and brush three times for a paler, softer top.
Signature drizzle sponge: use the drizzle on a plain sponge and serve with whipped cream.

title: Milk Sauces and Soups: Bechamel and Chowders
description: The Signature milk sauce is a two-stage design: a pale roux sauce finished with a cold-milk swirl, so the sauce arrives glossy rather than starchy. Stage one is a standard bechamel, cooked until it coats a spoon. Stage two, the Signature step, is 100 ml of ice-cold milk whisked in off the heat just before serving, which loosens the sauce to a pouring ribbon and brightens its flavor. The Signature chowder uses the same finish: the soup is simmered in stock, the milk is added late, and the cold swirl goes in at the table. The design rule is one sentence: cook the sauce hot, finish it cold. This is a Signature original method, not a traditional recipe record.
ingredients: 40 g butter, 40 g flour, 400 ml whole milk for cooking
100 ml ice-cold whole milk for the Signature finish
Salt, white pepper, a pinch of nutmeg
For Signature chowder: 500 g potatoes, 1 onion, 250 ml stock, 150 g corn, plus the same cold-milk finish
method: Cook the roux and whisk in the 400 ml of milk gradually, simmering until the sauce coats a spoon.
Take the pan off the heat and rest it for 2 minutes.
Whisk in the 100 ml of ice-cold milk in a thin stream until the sauce turns glossy and pourable.
Season, and serve at once; do not return the finished sauce to a hard boil.
For chowder, simmer the vegetables in stock, add the cooking milk, then finish with the cold swirl at the table.
safety: Use pasteurized milk. The cold-milk finish must itself be pasteurized milk, kept cold until use. Milk allergy and lactose notes apply, and leftovers must be refrigerated promptly.
storage: The Signature sauce keeps 2 days refrigerated; reheat gently and re-finish with a small splash of cold milk. Do not freeze the finished sauce, as the swirl texture breaks on thawing.
variations: Signature herb ribbon: whisk chopped herbs into the cold milk before the finish.
Signature cheese ribbon: melt 80 g cheese into the hot sauce before the cold finish.
Signature corn ribbon: blend the cold milk with 50 g corn kernels for a sweet finish.

title: Butter and Ghee Churning
description: The Signature churn is a two-cream design: half the cream is churned plain and half is cultured overnight, then the two butters are kneaded together in layers so each slice carries both a sweet and a tangy band. The Signature ghee follows the same pairing: plain ghee is infused with a toasted spice bundle, while a second small batch is left plain, and the two are poured into one jar in layers that set as a marbled fat. The design rule is pairing: never one butter when two layered butters tell the story. This is a Signature original design, not a traditional churning record.
ingredients: 500 ml cold heavy cream, plain
500 ml heavy cream plus 2 tablespoons cultured buttermilk, for the cultured half
Cold water for washing, salt to taste
For Signature ghee: 500 g butter and a spice bundle of cardamom, cinnamon, and clove
method: Stir the cultured buttermilk into the second 500 ml of cream and rest it covered at room temperature for 12 hours.
Churn each cream separately until each breaks into butter grains and buttermilk.
Wash and knead each butter separately, salting lightly.
Layer the two butters in a mold, pressing gently, and chill until firm.
For Signature ghee, simmer half the butter plain and half with the spice bundle, strain both, and pour into one jar in alternating layers.
safety: Use pasteurized cream. The cultured half ferments at room temperature only for the stated 12 hours; discard it if it smells sharply sour beyond a yogurt-like tang. Hot-fat rules apply to ghee exactly as in the plain method.
storage: Signature layered butter keeps 2 weeks refrigerated, frozen for months. Layered ghee keeps 3 months sealed at cool room temperature.
variations: Signature herb layer: replace the cultured half with herb butter for a green and gold layer.
Signature honey butter layer: knead honey into one half for a sweet layer, served with bread.
Signature plain-plus-spice ghee: pour the spice layer thin so the plain layer dominates.

title: Cream Products: Whipped, Clotted, Sour Cream, and Creme Fraiche
description: The Signature cream set is a four-way tasting board: whipped cream, clotted cream, sour cream, and creme fraiche served side by side from one cream source, so the taster compares all four textures at once. The Signature twist is a shared flavor thread: each of the four carries the same flavoring, for example vanilla, honey, or citrus zest, so the difference the taster notices is texture and tang alone. The board is assembled cold, with small spoons, and each cream is labeled by texture: airy, crusty, sharp, and mild. This is a Signature original presentation design, not a traditional cream record.
ingredients: 1 liter heavy cream, cold, plus 250 ml light cream
Flavor thread: 2 teaspoons vanilla extract, or 2 tablespoons honey, or the zest of one lemon
2 tablespoons cultured buttermilk for each cultured cream
Sugar to taste for the whipped cream
method: Divide the cream: 250 ml for whipping, 500 ml for clotting, 250 ml light cream for sour cream, and 250 ml heavy cream for creme fraiche.
Whip the first portion with the flavor thread and a little sugar until soft peaks form.
Clot the second portion by gentle long heating, chilling, and skimming, then stir in the same flavor thread.
Culture the third and fourth portions with buttermilk for 12 to 24 hours, then stir in the same flavor thread.
Arrange all four in small bowls on one board, label them airy, crusty, sharp, and mild, and serve cold with fruit or scones.
safety: Use pasteurized cream. Honey is not for infants under 12 months. Cultured portions follow the same discard rules as plain cultured cream.
storage: Assemble the board just before serving. Leftovers keep as their plain versions do: whipped cream hours, clotted cream 4 days, cultured creams 1 to 2 weeks, all refrigerated.
variations: Signature citrus thread: use lemon zest through all four for a bright board.
Signature honey thread: use honey through all four for a sweet board.
Signature berry board: serve the four creams with four different berries.

title: Fresh Cheeses: Ricotta, Paneer, Cottage Cheese, and Mozzarella
description: The Signature fresh cheese board pairs all four fresh cheeses in one sitting, each carrying a Signature flavor mark: ricotta with lemon zest, paneer with toasted spice, cottage cheese with herbs, and mozzarella with a honey drizzle. The Signature method is shared draining: all four curds are drained in one session, timed so the ricotta drains while the paneer presses and the mozzarella stretches last, when the hands are practiced. The board rule is contrast: soft against firm, mild against tangy, plain against marked, so a taster learns the whole fresh-cheese range from one board. This is a Signature original design, not a traditional cheese record.
ingredients: 4 liters whole milk, 2 liters whey
Lemon juice, vinegar, citric acid and rennet as needed
Signature marks: lemon zest, toasted cumin and coriander, chopped herbs, honey for drizzling
Salt and cloth for draining and pressing
method: Heat the milk and whey and form the ricotta first, scooping the flakes to drain.
Curdle the remaining milk with lemon juice for paneer, drain, and press with the toasted spice kneaded in.
Culture and set the cottage portion, cut, warm, and drain, then fold in herbs.
Stretch the mozzarella portion last in hot salted water, shape into balls, and drizzle with honey at serving.
Arrange all four on one board, label each, and serve within hours.
safety: Use pasteurized milk. Honey is not for infants under 12 months. Fresh-cheese storage and discard rules apply exactly as for plain fresh cheeses.
storage: Serve within hours. Leftovers keep 3 to 5 days refrigerated, mozzarella in brine, paneer wrapped, ricotta covered.
variations: Signature spice board: mark all four with the same toasted spice for a themed board.
Signature herb board: mark all four with herbs and serve with bread.
Signature sweet board: drizzle honey over the ricotta and mozzarella only.

title: Aged Cheeses: Cheddar, Gouda, and Brie Styles
description: The Signature aged trio ages three small wheels from one milk batch, one cheddar style, one gouda style, and one brie style, so the maker compares how the same milk turns out under three different handlings. The Signature step is a shared aging log: every wheel is weighed, turned, and tasted on the same days, and the log records rind, aroma, and texture at each check, so the trio teaches aging as a comparison rather than a wait. The cheddar wheel is pressed hardest, the gouda wheel is washed sweetest, and the brie wheel is ripened softest, and all three are cut on one tasting day. This is a Signature original design, not a traditional cheese record.
ingredients: 15 liters whole milk, divided into three 5-liter batches
Starter culture and rennet per the packet
Salt, cloth, a small press, molds, and a ripening box
A notebook or log sheet for the shared aging log
method: Make the three curds in one session, one per style, following the plain method for each.
Press the cheddar-style wheel hardest, wash the gouda-style curd warmest, and ladle the brie-style curd gentlest.
Start the shared log on pressing day: record weight, rind, and aroma for all three wheels.
Turn and check all three wheels on the same days each week, logging changes side by side.
Cut all three on one tasting day and compare firmness, aroma, and flavor in the log.
safety: Use pasteurized milk. The same mold and discard rules apply as for plain aged cheeses, and the log must record any wheel discarded and why.
storage: Keep the trio at 10 to 13 degrees Celsius while aging, then refrigerate cut pieces wrapped. Brie style is eaten first, gouda next, cheddar last.
variations: Signature single-milk tasting: use milk from one source for all three wheels to isolate handling effects.
Signature herb trio: add a different herb to each wheel before pressing or molding.
Signature mini trio: halve all quantities for three small wheels.

title: Yogurt and Cultured Milk: Yogurt, Kefir, and Cultured Buttermilk
description: The Signature cultured trio ferments yogurt, kefir, and cultured buttermilk from one milk source in one weekend, so the maker compares three cultures side by side. The Signature step is a shared tasting card: each culture is tasted at the same hour, and the card records thickness, tang, and aroma for all three, so the trio teaches culture behavior as a comparison. The yogurt is incubated warm, the kefir ferments at room temperature, and the buttermilk rests between them, and all three are chilled on the same evening. This is a Signature original design, not a traditional culture record.
ingredients: 3 liters whole milk, 1 liter per culture
2 tablespoons live plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon kefir grains, 2 tablespoons cultured buttermilk
Three clean jars, labels, and a tasting card
method: Heat the yogurt milk to 85 degrees Celsius, cool to 43 degrees, stir in the yogurt starter, and hold warm for 4 to 8 hours.
Start the kefir at the same time: grains into milk, covered loosely, at room temperature for about 24 hours.
Start the buttermilk at the same time: starter into milk, covered, at room temperature for 12 to 24 hours.
Taste all three at the same hour, record thickness, tang, and aroma on the card, then strain the kefir and refrigerate all three.
safety: Use pasteurized milk. The same discard rules apply as for plain cultured milk; the tasting card must record any batch discarded and why.
storage: All three keep 1 to 2 weeks refrigerated. Kefir grains are stored in fresh milk in the refrigerator between batches.
variations: Signature honey tasting: stir a little honey into each finished culture at tasting time; honey is not for infants under 12 months.
Signature fruit trio: add a different fruit to each culture at serving.
Signature thick trio: strain all three for a thick-style comparison.

title: Ice Cream and Frozen Desserts
description: The Signature frozen dessert is a layered ice cream cake built from one churned base in three flavors, stacked in a loaf tin so each slice shows three bands. The base is churned once, divided into three bowls, and flavored vanilla, chocolate, and honey-strawberry, then layered and frozen solid. The Signature step is the banding: each layer is frozen for 30 minutes before the next is poured, so the bands stay sharp instead of marbling. The cake is sliced with a hot knife and served with a spoon of whipped cream. This is a Signature original design, not a traditional ice cream record.
ingredients: 750 ml whole milk, 375 ml cream, 225 g sugar, 6 egg yolks for the base
Flavorings: vanilla, cocoa powder, honey and crushed strawberries
500 ml whipped cream for serving
A loaf tin lined with paper
method: Cook the custard base, chill it fully, and churn until thick and soft.
Divide the churned base into three bowls and flavor them vanilla, chocolate, and honey-strawberry.
Pour the chocolate layer into the lined tin and freeze 30 minutes.
Pour the vanilla layer over it and freeze 30 minutes, then pour the honey-strawberry layer and freeze until solid, at least 4 hours.
Unmold, slice with a hot knife, and serve with whipped cream.
safety: Use pasteurized milk and cream. Honey is not for infants under 12 months. Milk and egg allergy notes apply; keep the cake frozen and do not refreeze thawed slices.
storage: The layered cake keeps 2 to 3 weeks sealed in the freezer, best in the first week.
variations: Signature berry bands: use three berry flavors instead of vanilla, chocolate, and strawberry.
Signature honey bands: flavor all three layers with honey at different strengths.
Signature crunch bands: sprinkle crushed biscuits between layers before freezing.

title: Puddings and Custards: Rice Pudding, Panna Cotta, Creme Brulee, and Flan
description: The Signature pudding tower stacks all four puddings in one glass: rice pudding at the base, agar panna cotta in the middle, flan custard above it, and a brulee sugar shard on top. The Signature step is the build order: the rice pudding is chilled firm first, the panna cotta is poured over it and set, the flan custard is baked separately, cut into a disc, and laid on top, and the sugar shard is caramelized last and leaned against the glass. Each spoonful can take one layer or all four, so the tower teaches texture contrast: grainy, silky, smooth, and crisp. This is a Signature original design, not a traditional pudding record.
ingredients: Rice pudding base: 50 g rice, 500 ml milk, 30 g sugar
Agar panna cotta layer: 250 ml cream, 125 ml milk, 30 g sugar, 2 g agar powder
Flan disc: 250 ml milk, 2 eggs, 50 g sugar, 50 g sugar for caramel
Sugar shards: 60 g sugar, caramelized and cooled on paper
method: Cook the rice pudding, spoon it into four tall glasses, and chill until firm.
Make the agar panna cotta, pour it over the rice layer, and chill until set.
Bake the flan, chill it, and cut four discs to fit the glasses.
Lay one flan disc on each panna cotta layer.
Caramelize the sugar, cool it into shards, and lean one shard on each glass just before serving.
safety: Use pasteurized milk and cream. Agar is the gelling agent; gelatin is excluded. Egg custards must be baked until set and refrigerated promptly. Sugar shards are hot when made and must cool fully before handling.
storage: Assemble the tower the day it is served; the layers keep 2 days refrigerated without the shard, and the shard is added at serving so it stays crisp.
variations: Signature berry tower: add a berry layer between the panna cotta and the flan.
Signature honey tower: drizzle honey over the flan disc; honey is not for infants under 12 months.
Signature chocolate tower: add cocoa to the panna cotta layer.

title: Milk Drinks: Lattes, Milkshakes, Lassi, Honey Milk, and Chocolate Milk
description: The Signature milk drink flight serves four small milk drinks side by side: a mini latte, a mini milkshake, a mini lassi, and a mini honey milk, so the drinker compares coffee, ice cream, yogurt, and honey carriers in one sitting. The Signature step is a shared milk base: all four drinks start from the same milk, measured from one jug, so the flight teaches how one ingredient changes character with four partners. The flight is served on one tray with four small glasses, labeled in order from lightest to richest. This is a Signature original design, not a traditional drink record.
ingredients: 1 liter whole milk, pasteurized
Espresso for the latte glass, ice cream for the shake glass, yogurt for the lassi glass, honey and cinnamon for the honey milk glass
Four small glasses and one tray
method: Measure 250 ml of milk for each of the four drinks from one jug.
Make the mini latte with espresso and steamed milk.
Blend the mini milkshake with milk and ice cream.
Whisk the mini lassi with milk and yogurt.
Warm the mini honey milk and stir in honey and cinnamon.
Arrange the four glasses on one tray, label them lightest to richest, and serve at once.
safety: Use pasteurized milk and yogurt. Honey is not for infants under 12 months. The latte glass contains caffeine. Serve the flight promptly and keep the cold glasses cold.
storage: The flight is served fresh and is not stored. Leftovers of any single drink keep a few hours refrigerated.
variations: Signature iced flight: serve all four drinks over ice in warm weather.
Signature fruit flight: add a different fruit to the shake and lassi glasses.
Signature spice flight: spice all four glasses with cinnamon at different strengths.

title: Condensed and Evaporated Milk, and Milk Powder
description: The Signature preserved milk trio makes all three preserved milks from one milk source in one session: a small jar of evaporated milk, a small jar of sweetened condensed milk, and a pouch of dried milk powder made by low-oven drying for demonstration. The Signature step is a shared label set: each container is labeled with its starting milk volume, its finished volume or weight, and its reduction ratio, so the trio teaches preservation as arithmetic. The trio is tasted side by side: the evaporated milk in coffee, the condensed milk on bread, and the reconstituted milk in a glass. This is a Signature original design, not a traditional preservation record.
ingredients: 3 liters whole milk, 1 liter per preserved form
200 g sugar for the condensed jar
Three clean containers and labels
method: Simmer the first liter gently until reduced to about 400 ml for evaporated milk, then cool and jar it.
Simmer the second liter with sugar until thick and reduced to about 400 ml for condensed milk, then cool and jar it.
Dry the third liter by a low-oven demonstration method, or use purchased milk powder for the pouch, and label it with its reconstitution ratio.
Label all three with starting volume, finished volume or weight, and reduction ratio.
Taste all three side by side as described and refrigerate the jars.
safety: Use pasteurized milk. Home drying does not match spray-dried powder for shelf life, so the demonstration pouch is used within days and kept dry. Refrigerate the jars promptly.
storage: The trio jars keep 5 to 7 days refrigerated; the demonstration pouch keeps days sealed and dry. Commercial canned and powdered versions keep as their labels state.
variations: Signature coffee trio: taste all three in coffee instead of plain.
Signature dessert trio: taste all three in desserts.
Signature label trio: add a tasting note to each label.

demo.code:

title: Casein Glue and Milk Paint: Historical Craft
description: The Signature casein craft set pairs a wood glue joint with a painted panel from the same milk batch, so the maker proves the binder twice: once as glue, once as paint. The Signature step is the test pair: two identical wood joints are glued, one with casein glue and one with plain milk curd paste, and the maker compares which holds after a day, learning why the alkali step matters. The painted panel carries the same binder as the glue joint, in a Signature color mixed from two pigments, so the set shows one material doing two jobs. This is a Signature original design, not a traditional craft record.
ingredients: 2 liters skim milk, 120 ml vinegar, lime or borax, water
Two pigments for the Signature color, wood offcuts for joints and a panel, a brush, clamps
Gloves and eye protection
method: Curdle and drain both liters of milk into casein curd.
Dissolve one batch of curd with lime or borax into glue; leave the second batch as plain curd paste for comparison.
Glue two identical joints, one with each binder, clamp, and rest for 24 hours.
Mix the remaining glue into paint with the two Signature pigments and paint the panel in thin coats.
Test both joints the next day, record which held, and keep the panel as the color sample.
safety: Use pasteurized milk. Lime rules apply exactly as in the plain method. Glue and paint are not food and must be labeled. Keep the work away from children.
storage: Mix fresh for the set; discard leftover glue and paint after a few days refrigerated. The glued joints and painted panel keep as craft pieces.
variations: Signature color set: mix three pigment pairs for three panels from one glue batch.
Signature joint set: test three joint shapes with the same glue.
Signature sealed panel: seal the panel with beeswax polish for a finished craft.

title: Whey Uses: Whey Drinks, Whey Ricotta, and Whey in Baking
description: The Signature whey day uses one cheese batch's whey three ways in one day: a whey drink at midday, whey ricotta in the afternoon, and whey bread for the evening, so nothing from the cheese batch is wasted. The Signature step is the whey ledger: the maker records the milk volume, the cheese weight, and the whey volume, then records how much whey each of the three uses consumed, so the day ends with a closed account of the whole batch. The drink uses the freshest whey, the ricotta uses the reheated whey, and the bread uses the last of it, in that order. This is a Signature original design, not a traditional whey record.
ingredients: Whey from a 10-liter cheese batch, about 9 liters
Fruit juice and sweetener for the drink, lemon juice for the ricotta, flour and yeast for the bread
A ledger sheet for the whey account
method: Make the cheese batch and record the milk volume, cheese weight, and whey volume in the ledger.
Chill 500 ml of whey for the midday drink with juice and sweetener.
Reheat 2 liters of whey with a little milk and acid for afternoon ricotta, and record the yield.
Use 300 ml of whey in place of water for the evening bread, and record the amount.
Close the ledger: total whey used against whey recovered, and freeze or use the remainder within days.
safety: Use whey from pasteurized milk cheese. The same allergy, honey, and discard rules apply as for plain whey uses.
storage: The whey day's products keep as their plain versions do: drink 2 to 3 days, ricotta 3 to 5 days, bread 2 to 3 days, all refrigerated except bread at room temperature.
variations: Signature whey week: spread the three uses across a week instead of a day.
Signature whey ledger board: post the ledger in the kitchen for the next cheese batch.
Signature whey feast: add whey pancakes to the day as a fourth use.

title: Milk Preservation: Pasteurization, UHT, and Fermentation Preservation
description: The Signature preservation plan is a household milk calendar: one week's milk is divided at purchase into drinking milk, culturing milk, and cooking milk, with a date label on each container and a rule for what happens when each date passes. The Signature step is the rollover rule: drinking milk that nears its date is cultured into yogurt, yogurt that nears its date is baked into bread, and bread that nears its date is frozen, so milk moves down a ladder of uses instead of being thrown away. The calendar is written on one card on the refrigerator, with three columns, one per use, and the rollover arrow between them. This is a Signature original design, not a traditional preservation record.
ingredients: One week's milk supply, pasteurized
Live yogurt starter for the culturing column
Flour, yeast, and salt for the baking column
Labels and one calendar card
method: Divide the week's milk at purchase: drinking milk, culturing milk, and cooking milk, and label each with its date.
Drink the drinking milk first, within its date.
Culture the culturing milk into yogurt before its date passes.
Bake the yogurt into bread before the yogurt date passes, and freeze any bread not eaten in 2 days.
Move any leftover milk down the ladder at each step instead of discarding it, and record each move on the calendar card.
safety: Use pasteurized milk. The rollover rule never extends a date: each move happens before the current date passes, and anything that smells or tastes wrong is discarded at once. Milk allergy and lactose notes apply to every column.
storage: Drinking milk: to its date refrigerated. Yogurt: 1 to 2 weeks refrigerated. Bread: 2 to 3 days at room temperature, frozen for a month.
variations: Signature surplus week: add a cheese column for weeks with extra milk.
Signature UHT backup: keep one unopened UHT carton as the calendar's reserve.
Signature freezer column: freeze surplus milk in portions for cooking.
